cases.label: Case 1: tracker-dependent gap at the line
cases.observed_failure: In MVI_63553, GT vehicle 73 crosses the line at frame 527. YOLOv8n + BoT-SORT keeps ID 273 through frame 526, loses it at 527 and 528, and resumes it at 529. No crossing event is produced. YOLOv8n + ByteTrack and both YOLOv8s configurations count the same vehicle once at 527.
cases.likely_cause: The confirmed counting mechanism is a gap of three frames between adjacent observations across the line, exceeding max_frame_gap=1. Motion blur, overlapping neighbouring cars and uncertain detections plausibly make association difficult. In the GPU diagnostic, the best-overlap YOLOv8n car detections score 0.239, 0.258 and 0.206 at 526-528, while YOLOv8s scores 0.781, 0.791 and 0.661. Low-score detections reach both trackers in the current protocol; the difference is therefore compatible with tracker association and motion compensation interacting with weaker detections.
cases.cause_confidence: High for the observed gap and counting-rule mechanism; moderate for the upstream association explanation.
cases.counting_impact: One missed car and signed all-class error -1 for YOLOv8n + BoT-SORT on this vehicle. The other three configurations have zero local count error.
cases.limitations: The original raw detections and tracker association matrices were not saved. The probe repeats isolated frames and does not identify the exact failed association or isolate GMC from other tracker differences. Nearby boxes overlap, so automatic identity evidence alone is insufficient. This selected example does not establish the frequency of this cause across dev.
cases.possible_improvement: On dev, compare bounded gap handling using the same counting rule for GT and predictions, or inspect association/GMC behaviour. Evaluate false crossings before changing the current max_frame_gap=1 rule.

cases.label: Case 2: van mapping and track class aggregation
cases.observed_failure: In MVI_20033, GT vehicle 11 is a van mapped to car. YOLOv8n + ByteTrack counts ID 65 as truck at frame 278; the GT crossing is at 279. All other configurations count the vehicle once as car. ByteTrack ID 65 has 11 truck, 6 car and 5 bus observations, while BoT-SORT ID 58 has 173 car, 29 truck and 3 bus observations.
cases.likely_cause: The predefined van-to-car mapping differs from the ambiguous COCO appearance of a van. Classification varies over time, and the counter assigns the most frequent class over the complete saved track. Different track histories change that majority. The probe at frame 279 returns YOLOv8n truck 0.424 and car 0.208 on the same van; this supports class ambiguity, while the saved votes directly explain the different event labels.
cases.cause_confidence: High for the class-vote mechanism and the error relative to the agreed label mapping. The physical vehicle type is a van, not evidence that COCO semantic categories are unambiguous.
cases.counting_impact: YOLOv8n + ByteTrack has one missing car and one extra truck, with zero all-class count error for this vehicle. The other configurations have zero local class/count error.
cases.limitations: Majority voting uses the complete track, so a box labelled truck at the crossing can still lead to a car event. Per-class counts are sensitive to dataset mapping. There is only one GT truck crossing in the dev subset; general truck-class conclusions are unsupported.
cases.possible_improvement: Investigate class-stability strategies and review van/others mapping limitations using the same mapping for all configurations. Do not relabel individual examples to improve scores.

cases.label: Case 3: simultaneous tracks and double counting
cases.observed_failure: In MVI_40141, GT van 10 crosses at frame 141. Both YOLOv8s trackers maintain two simultaneous overlapping IDs and count both: ByteTrack IDs 40 and 136 produce car and truck events; BoT-SORT IDs 41 and 135 produce two car events. Both YOLOv8n configurations count ID 28 once.
cases.likely_cause: The same physical van receives overlapping car and truck detections, which class-aware NMS can preserve. The GPU probe at frame 141 returns car confidence 0.496 and truck confidence 0.525, both with IoU about 0.91 against the GT box. Both trackers retain duplicate identities and the ID-based counter counts each trajectory once. BoT-SORT ID 135 has 3 car and 1 truck observations, explaining why its event is car despite the truck box visible on that frame.
cases.cause_confidence: High for the observed double count and retained duplicate trajectories; supported but qualified detector/NMS explanation from the isolated-frame replay.
cases.counting_impact: One extra all-class event for each YOLOv8s configuration on this van. ByteTrack adds one truck; BoT-SORT adds one car. The YOLOv8n configurations have zero local count error.
cases.limitations: Concurrent duplicate tracks are not equivalent to an official ID switch. This example does not show that class-agnostic NMS improves aggregate counting accuracy. The controlled dev NMS comparison gave a slightly better mean counting MAE for class-aware NMS, so the selected current policy is preserved.
cases.possible_improvement: Evaluate conservative duplicate-trajectory filtering on dev while protecting nearby real vehicles. Any NMS change needs a controlled aggregate comparison; no such pipeline change is applied here.
